passages.title: Leaves That Moved Empires
passages.passage:
Few drinks have travelled as far as tea, and fewer still have altered the fortunes of so many nations along the way. According to one account, the leaves were first brewed by accident (1)____ than by design, when a few of them drifted into a pot of water being boiled beneath a tree. Whether or not the story is true, tea (2)____ certainly been cultivated in the hills of south-west China for well over two thousand years. For most of that time it remained a local pleasure; not (3)____ the ninth century did it become a commodity worth carrying across mountains on the backs of mules. Compressed into bricks, it was traded for horses along a route so arduous that some porters carried loads heavier (4)____ themselves.

When European merchants eventually (5)____ across the drink in the early seventeenth century, they had no idea what to make of it. Within a hundred years, however, the British were importing it (6)____ such quantities that the government came to depend on the tax it yielded. This dependence had consequences (7)____ which nobody had planned. Smuggling flourished, colonies protested, and one famous cargo ended up in a harbour rather than in a teapot. Had the tax been lighter, the course of at least one revolution (8)____ have run differently.

Today tea is grown on every inhabited continent and drunk more widely than any beverage (9)____ water. Global commodity (10)____ it now is, it has kept a curious intimacy: whatever the country, offering someone a cup still signals that they are welcome to stay.

questions.explanation: The fixed contrast is by accident rather than by design. More than by design would compare degrees, not replace one cause with the other, and other than means apart from, which is not the meaning here.

For well over two thousand years stretches from the past up to now, so the present perfect has been cultivated is required. Was would close the period in the past, and had needs a later past event to be earlier than.
Not until + time, fronted for emphasis, triggers the inversion did it become. Before cannot follow not in this fronted pattern, and in would make not in the ninth century a plain denial.
The comparative heavier must be completed with than. As pairs only with the equal form as heavy as, and to follows superior or inferior, never an -er comparative.
To meet something by chance is to come across it (also stumble, run or happen across). Found and discovered take a direct object and cannot be followed by across.
Amounts are expressed with in such quantities, just as in in large numbers. With or at do not collocate with quantities in this sense.

You plan for a consequence, so the relative clause keeps that preposition: consequences for which nobody had planned. Of which would need a verb like thought, and which alone leaves planned with a false object.
Had the tax been lighter is an inverted third conditional, so the result needs a past modal: might (or would/could) have run. Will or can would describe a real future, not a lost past possibility.
After any beverage the exclusion is marked by except (also but, save, bar, besides). Than has already been used with more widely, and without would mean the tea contained no water.
When a noun or adjective is fronted for concession, only though or as can follow it: Global commodity though it now is. Although and despite cannot take this inverted position.

passages.title: A Compass the Size of a Seed
passages.passage:
A honeybee on a foraging trip may travel several kilometres, visit hundreds of flowers and still find its way home with uncanny accuracy. How it manages this has puzzled naturalists (1)____ centuries. Only in recent decades have the pieces of the answer begun to fall (2)____ place.

The first clue lies in the sun. Bees perceive polarised light, a pattern invisible to us, (3)____ allows them to work out the sun's position even when it is hidden behind cloud. The second is an internal clock: because the sun moves, a bee that set out at nine must correct its bearings by noon, and it does so effortlessly. (4)____ far a bee may fly from the hive, its brain keeps a running tally of every turn and every straight stretch.

This tally is what makes the famous waggle dance work. A successful forager dances on the comb, and the angle of her run tells her sisters (5)____ direction to fly relative to the sun. The length of the run indicates the distance. Were the dance merely a display of excitement, other bees (6)____ hardly be able to locate a food source they had never seen.

Landmarks matter too. Near home, bees rely (7)____ familiar features such as trees and hedges, which is why a hive moved even a few metres can leave its residents circling in confusion. What is remarkable is the way these abilities are combined: an insect with a brain the size of a seed integrates light, time and memory (8)____ one coherent map. Scientists are now asking (9)____ damage to this navigation, blamed partly on pesticides, accounts for the decline in colonies across Europe and North America. Should the answer turn (10)____ to be yes, the consequences for crops that depend on pollination could be severe.

questions.explanation: Centuries is a length of time, so the present perfect takes for. Since needs a starting point such as since 1700, and during does not combine with a bare plural of duration here.
When separate facts start to make sense together, they fall into place. In place describes something already fixed, so it cannot follow the movement verb fall in this idiom.
The clause adds extra information after a comma, so it is non-defining and takes which. That is not used in non-defining clauses, and it would create a run-on sentence.
However far a bee may fly means no matter how far: however + adverb introduces a concessive clause. Although cannot be followed directly by far, and whatever needs a noun.
Tells her sisters is followed by an embedded question, so which (or what) direction to fly. The would need a full relative clause, and where cannot precede the noun direction.
Were the dance merely a display is an inverted second conditional, so the main clause needs would (or could) hardly be able. Will belongs to a real condition, which this hypothesis is not.
The verb is rely on (or upon) something. Rely in and rely with do not exist, and rely to confuses the verb with refer to.

Separate things are integrated into a single whole: the preposition expresses the result of combining. In would locate the map rather than describe its formation, and as would wrongly equate the inputs with the map.
Asking introduces an indirect yes/no question, so whether (or if) is needed. That would turn the open question into a statement, and how would ask for a method, not a yes/no answer.
Turn out to be means to prove in the end to be. Turn up means to appear unexpectedly, and turn into means to change into something, neither of which takes to be.

passages.title: Streets Given Back
passages.passage:
Imagine a city where the loudest sound at rush hour is the ringing of bicycle bells. It sounds like a utopian fantasy, (1)____ a handful of places have come surprisingly close to it. One Spanish town closed its historic centre to private vehicles in the late 1990s, at a time (2)____ such a decision was regarded as political suicide. Shopkeepers predicted ruin. Instead, footfall rose, air pollution fell by two thirds and, contrary (3)____ every expectation, the town became a model that delegations from abroad now come to study.

The reasoning behind such schemes is simple. Cars take up an astonishing amount of space for the number of people they move, so much (4)____ that in some cities up to eighty percent of urban land is given over to roads and parking. Reclaim even a fraction, and daily life is transformed. Streets that once served as corridors turn (5)____ places where people linger, and struggling shops suddenly find customers in no hurry to be elsewhere.

The objections, (6)____, are not trivial. Deliveries must still be made, the elderly cannot always cycle, and residents of the suburbs, for (7)____ a car is often the only realistic option, may feel that a privilege is being withdrawn for the benefit of people wealthy enough to live centrally. Any council that ignores these concerns does so (8)____ its peril. What the successful examples have in common is that they moved gradually, one street at a time, and that public transport (9)____ been improved before the first barrier went up.

No sooner had the first fully car-free district opened in a large European city (10)____ property prices there began to climb. Whether that is a sign of success or a warning about who really benefits is a question planners are still debating.

questions.explanation: The second clause contradicts the first, so a contrastive conjunction is needed: yet or but. So would present the near-success as a result of its being a fantasy, and and loses the contrast entirely.
After a time the relative adverb is when. Which would need the preposition, as in at which, and where refers to places, not periods.
The fixed phrase is contrary to expectation. Contrary with and contrary of do not exist; the noun form would be on the contrary, which does not fit here.
So much so that intensifies a previous statement before giving its consequence. So much that alone would need a verb to modify, and so much as that is not a linking expression.
A change of state is turn into: corridors become places to linger. Turn to means to seek help from someone, and turn in means to hand over or go to bed.

A contrast with the previous paragraph, set between commas inside the sentence, calls for however (or though, nevertheless, nonetheless; the concessive admittedly also fits). But and although are conjunctions and cannot sit in this parenthetical slot.
Directly after a preposition the relative pronoun must be the object form whom: for whom a car is the only option. Who is not used after for, and which cannot refer to people.
The idiom is at one's peril, meaning with a risk of harm to oneself. In peril describes a state of danger and cannot take the possessive its in this warning sense.

The improvement was completed before a past event, went up, so the past perfect had been improved is required. Has been would clash with the past tense of the following clause, and was been is not a form.

The inverted pattern No sooner had X happened is completed with than, because sooner is a comparative. When belongs with hardly or scarcely, and then is a common misspelling that breaks the structure.

passages.title: The Office Comes Home
passages.passage:
Until quite recently, the idea that a large share of office work could be done from a kitchen table was dismissed as wishful thinking. Managers took it (1)____ granted that productivity would collapse the moment staff were out of sight. Few companies, therefore, were willing to put the theory (2)____ the test. Then circumstances forced their hand. Within weeks, millions of employees who had never worked a day from home were doing so full-time, and the results, (3)____ patchy, were far better than the pessimists had predicted.

Several years (4)____, the picture is more complicated. Some firms have called their staff back, arguing that innovation depends on the chance conversations that only happen when people share a corridor. Others have (5)____ office space altogether and now recruit from anywhere with a reliable connection. (6)____, the majority lie somewhere in between, with a hybrid arrangement that satisfies nobody completely but that few are prepared to abandon.

What is (7)____ dispute is that the change has altered the balance of power. Workers who once accepted a two-hour commute as an unavoidable fact of life now regard it as a cost to be weighed against the salary on offer, and employers who insist on five days in the office find their pool of candidates (8)____ accordingly. The effects reach well beyond the workplace: city-centre cafés have lost their lunchtime trade, while small towns within commuting distance have gained residents who would never (9)____ considered living there.

(10)____ remains to be seen is whether the arrangement will survive the next downturn, when the bargaining power that made it possible may shift back the other way.

questions.q: Blank (1): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The idiom is take it for granted that, meaning to assume without question. Take as needs a noun such as a compliment, and on and by never follow take it before granted.

questions.q: Blank (2): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: You put something to the test when you try it out for real. Under test would need is rather than put, and on and in do not form this expression.

questions.q: Blank (3): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Albeit can be followed directly by an adjective to concede a weakness: the results, albeit patchy, were better. Despite needs a noun or being, even would need if, and whereas requires a full clause.

questions.q: Blank (4): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The sentence describes the present situation, so several years later moves the narrative forward to now. Ago and before point backwards, and since cannot stand alone after a period of time in this position.

questions.q: Blank (5): choose the words that fit.
questions.explanation: To manage without something is to dispense with it. Dispense takes no other preposition in this sense; dispose of is a different verb, and from and for form no phrasal verb with dispense.

questions.q: Blank (6): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Meanwhile is an adverb that opens a complete sentence and sets the majority alongside the two extremes just described. Whereas and although would leave the sentence as a fragment with no main clause, and despite cannot be followed by a subject and verb.

questions.q: Blank (7): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Something nobody can argue with is beyond dispute. Over and against describe the position of the parties in an argument, not the certainty of a fact, and across dispute is not English.

questions.q: Blank (8): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: After find + object, a present participle describes what the object is doing: find their pool shrinking. A finite verb such as shrinks or shrank would need its own subject, and find X to shrink is not idiomatic.

questions.q: Blank (9): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: A past unreal idea uses modal + have + past participle: would never have considered. Had and has cannot follow a modal, and having would need be before it.

questions.q: Blank (10): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: A cleft sentence begins with What as the subject of its own clause: What remains to be seen is whether. It remains to be seen would need no is, that cannot open a subject clause without a verb after it, and which requires a preceding noun.
